facts.fact: Tom Allen said he would meet Charley Gallagher at any place Gallagher named to draw up articles, if Gallagher covered a $200 deposit.
Tom Allen challenged Charley Gallagher to fight for $500, apart from his McCoole match, and deposited $100 with his backer Billy Carroll for Gallagher to cover.
Tom Allen and Charley Gallagher made a match for $500 a side and the excursion money, to be fought on August 17 within fifty miles of St. Louis.
Ben Hogan arrived in St. Louis and said he was willing to fight Tom Allen.
Patsey Reardon published a challenge in a St. Louis paper to fight Tom Allen.
Jim Coyne challenged Ben Hogan to fight four weeks after the Allen and Gallagher fight, for $500 or $1,000 a side.

After Allen and Gallagher's fight, Gallagher proposed a return fight for the same stakes plus about $1,000 a side, and Tom Allen accepted it around August 20, 1869; Allen was to name a place within fifty miles of Cincinnati and meet Gallagher on Saturday afternoon to draw up articles.
facts.conflict: stakes added: $1,000 a side (356.c4, 359.c5) vs $1,900 (360.c1, low, printed as $1,900); Sherman Thurston (359.c6, medium) said Allen had to fight McCoole before any other engagement, while 359.c5 says Allen accepted; 363.c5 (medium) says Allen was already under engagement to McCoole when Gallagher asked for a meeting; 356.c4 is dated Aug 18 and 360.c3 says the meeting was on Saturday Aug 21

facts.fact: Joe Wormald wrote to Tom Allen asking him to arrange the preliminaries of a match with Ned O'Baldwin for $5,000 a side.
Jack Looney offered to back Charley Gallagher against Tom Allen for any amount once Gallagher recovered.
A deposit for the Mike McCoole and Tom Allen match was put up at Allen's saloon on the night of October 9, 1869.
facts.conflict: stake per side: $599 (369.c1, medium, printed as $599, and said to be a deposit that was to be made) vs $500 (370.c1, medium, said to have been put up)

facts.fact: Tom Allen and Mike McCoole negotiated a match for the championship of America, set for November 10, 1869, and it did not take place.
facts.conflict: stakes: $5,000 (094.c6, 374.c3) vs excursion money (024.c6, 374.c4); cause: match fell through over a final stakeholder (094.c6, retrospective) vs McCoole refusing anything but $5,000 stakes (374.c3); 356.c5 (medium) puts an expected November fight in a claim published Aug 19, 1869, before the October deposit, and calls it doubtful

facts.fact: Tom Allen announced he would fight any man in America for $500 to $10,000 in a square stand-up fight under London prize ring rules.
facts.conflict: scope: any man in America (025.c1) vs any man in the world (026.c2, medium); 026.c2 also says Allen wanted time for preliminaries

facts.fact: Tom Allen offered to meet Joe Coburn in the ring anywhere in Wyoming Territory, whom he called the leading scientific pugilist in the United States.
Tom Allen, through Billy Carroll, offered to fight Jem Mace for $2,500 a side, six months from signing articles, and in late December forwarded forfeit money accepting Mace's challenge.
facts.conflict: stake: a telegram reported Allen matched with Mace for $5,000 a side, which Allen's backers denied (026.c1, medium, dated Dec 10) vs $2,500 (377.c2); forfeit: $500 (377.c3, low, printed as $5€0) vs $690 (379.c4, low, printed as $690); place: Pittsburgh (377.c3, low) vs New York (379.c2, 286.c1), with Allen not inclined to go to New York until he knew Mace's terms (286.c1, Dec 28)

facts.fact: Tom Allen apparently accepted Joe Coburn's challenge to fight for $10,000, although the report is garbled.
facts.conflict: 376.c1 is low confidence and only reports apparent acceptance; 025.c2 records only Allen's offer to meet Coburn

facts.fact: Tom Allen and Jem Mace each deposited $500 with a stakeholder, and Mace offered to meet Allen in New York and pay half his expenses there, after the Clipper reported that Mace accepted Allen's challenge.
facts.conflict: belt stake proposed by Mace's New York friends (379.c3) is medium confidence and not confirmed by the other claims
